**My thinking as this farmer:**

I am 67 now, and my back is not what it used to be. A few of my sons and daughters-in-law work in Handan or further away, so during planting and harvest I mostly rely on myself and one or two family members who stay home, plus I hire some help when the machines come through the village. I have been doing this same wheat-maize rotation for many years. I know this land.

My 16.1 mu, I split it the same way I have for years: about 10 mu for the wheat-maize rotation, and the remaining 6.1 mu I keep in cotton. Cotton is more trouble — lots of spraying, lots of watching — but the cash income matters and I know cotton well. Grain is steady food security.

For wheat, I buy the improved certified seed from the township seed shop, same variety as my neighbors use. I apply compound fertilizer at sowing and urea at jointing. I irrigate three times: once before sowing to ensure germination, once at the jointing stage, and once at grain filling. I use a rotary tiller after maize harvest to prepare the seedbed.

For maize, I plant straight after wheat harvest in June without plowing — no time and the ground is already worked. I use hybrid seed, which everyone does now. I apply fertilizer at planting and again when the plant is knee-high. Summer rain usually helps, but I run the well pump twice if it stays dry.

For cotton, I plow in spring, transplant or direct-sow in late April. Cotton needs potassium and pest management. I spray four times through the season — mostly for aphids, mites, and bollworm. I irrigate four times from the well.

I do not change much year to year. What worked before, I do again.
